problems.name: Subsets
problems.question: Given an integer array nums with unique elements, return all possible subsets. The solution set must not contain duplicate subsets.
problems.constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 10; -10 <= nums[i] <= 10; all elements are unique.

examples.explanation: Each number is either chosen or skipped.
There are two subsets for one element.
There are four subsets.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n * 2^n); Space O(n * 2^n). Iterative expansion doubles the result set for each number.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n * 2^n); Space O(n) recursion stack excluding output.

problems.name: Subsets II
problems.question: Given an integer array nums that may contain duplicates, return all possible subsets without duplicate subsets.

examples.explanation: The duplicate subset [2] appears only once.
One element still has two subsets.
Only different counts of value 2 matter.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n * 2^n); Space O(n * 2^n). Iterative expansion only extends subsets created in the previous round for duplicates.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n * 2^n); Space O(n) stack excluding output. Sorted backtracking skips same-depth duplicates.

problems.name: Permutations
problems.question: Given an array nums of distinct integers, return all possible permutations.
problems.constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 6; -10 <= nums[i] <= 10; all values are unique.

examples.explanation: All 3! orderings are returned.
Two values have two orders.
One value has one permutation.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n! * n); Space O(n! * n). Iterative insertion builds permutations level by level.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n! * n); Space O(n) stack excluding output.

problems.name: Permutations II
problems.question: Given a collection of numbers nums that may contain duplicates, return all unique permutations.

examples.explanation: Duplicate 1 values do not create duplicate permutations.
With all unique values, all 3! permutations appear.
Only one unique ordering exists.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(uniquePermutations * n); Space O(uniquePermutations * n). Iterative insertion skips same insertion positions for duplicates.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(uniquePermutations * n); Space O(n) stack excluding output.

problems.name: Combinations
problems.question: Given n and k, return all possible combinations of k numbers chosen from 1 to n.

examples.explanation: Every size-2 choice is listed.
Only one number exists.
Choosing all numbers gives one combination.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(C(n,k) * k); Space O(k) stack state excluding output.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(C(n,k) * k); Space O(k) recursion stack excluding output.

problems.name: Combination Sum
problems.question: Given distinct candidates and a target, return all unique combinations where chosen numbers sum to target. The same number may be chosen unlimited times.
problems.constraints: 1 <= candidates.length <= 30; 2 <= candidates[i] <= 40; candidates are distinct; 1 <= target <= 40.

examples.explanation: 2 can be reused and 7 is exact.
All combinations sum to 8.
No combination can reach 1.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time exponential in output size; Space O(target/minCandidate). Iterative stack applies sorted pruning.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time exponential in output size; Space O(target/minCandidate). Backtracking prunes candidates above remaining target.

problems.name: Combination Sum II
problems.question: Given candidates that may contain duplicates and a target, return all unique combinations where each candidate may be used at most once.

examples.explanation: Each index is used at most once.
Duplicate 2 values are handled without duplicate combinations.
The only candidate is too large.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(2^n); Space O(n). Iterative stack with sorted duplicate pruning.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(2^n); Space O(n). Backtracking skips same-depth duplicates and prunes large values.

problems.name: Combination Sum III
problems.question: Find all valid combinations of k numbers that sum to n using only numbers 1 through 9, where each number is used at most once.

examples.explanation: Only 1 + 2 + 4 equals 7.
Three valid size-3 combinations exist.
The target is too small for four positive numbers.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(C(9,k)); Space O(k). Iterative stack prunes by remaining count and sum.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(C(9,k)); Space O(k). Backtracking prunes candidates greater than remaining sum.

problems.name: Generate Parentheses
problems.question: Given n pairs of parentheses, generate all combinations of well-formed parentheses.

examples.explanation: All valid strings with three pairs are generated.
Only one valid string exists.
Two valid strings exist.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(Cn * n); Space O(Cn * n). Iterative stack explores only valid prefixes.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(Cn * n); Space O(n) stack excluding output.

problems.name: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
problems.question: Given a string digits containing digits 2 through 9, return all possible letter combinations the number could represent.

examples.explanation: Every 2-letter choice combines with every 3-letter choice.
No digits means no combinations.
Digit 2 maps to three letters.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(4^n * n); Space O(4^n * n). Queue expansion processes one digit level at a time.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(4^n * n); Space O(n) stack excluding output.

source.label: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number - LeetCode 17

problems.name: Palindrome Partitioning
problems.question: Given a string s, partition it so that every substring in the partition is a palindrome. Return all possible palindrome partitionings.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 16; s contains lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: Both partitions contain only palindromes.
A single character is a palindrome.
The whole string is also a palindrome.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n * 2^n); Space O(n^2). Iterative stack uses precomputed palindrome table.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n * 2^n); Space O(n^2 + n). Backtracking uses a palindrome DP table.

problems.name: Restore IP Addresses
problems.question: Given a string containing only digits, return all possible valid IP addresses that can be formed by inserting three dots.

examples.explanation: Both addresses have four valid segments.
Each segment is a single zero.
Multiple segment lengths are valid.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(1); Space O(1). Iterative loops choose three cut positions with pruning.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(1); Space O(1). Backtracking depth is fixed at four segments.

problems.name: Word Search
problems.question: Given an m x n character board and a word, return true if the word exists in the grid by adjacent horizontal or vertical moves without reusing cells.

examples.explanation: A valid adjacent path spells the word.
SEE exists on the board.
The path would need to reuse B.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(m*n*3^L); Space O(L). Iterative DFS avoids revisiting cells already in the path.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(m*n*3^L); Space O(L). In-place marking keeps visited state compact.

problems.name: N-Queens
problems.question: Given n, return all distinct boards that place n queens on an n x n board so no two queens attack each other.

examples.explanation: The classic 4-queens puzzle has two solutions.
One queen is valid.
No valid placement exists.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n!); Space O(n). Iterative row search maintains constraint arrays.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n!); Space O(n). Backtracking places one queen per row.

problems.name: Sudoku Solver
problems.question: Solve a 9 x 9 Sudoku board by filling empty cells marked with dots. The given board has exactly one solution.
problems.constraints: board is 9 x 9; cells are digits 1..9 or dot; the puzzle has exactly one solution.

examples.explanation: All rows, columns, and boxes become valid.
The only valid digit is inserted.
No search is needed.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(9^e); Space O(e). Iterative stack uses precomputed constraints.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(9^e); Space O(e). Backtracking with constraint tables tests digits in O(1).

problems.name: Rat in a Maze
problems.question: Given an n x n maze matrix where 1 means open and 0 means blocked, return all paths from top-left to bottom-right using moves D, L, R, and U without revisiting cells.
problems.constraints: 1 <= n <= 5 in common interview variants; mat[i][j] is 0 or 1.

examples.explanation: Two valid paths reach the bottom-right cell.
The destination is isolated.
The rat starts at the destination.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(4^(n^2)); Space O(n^2). Iterative DFS stores path and visited mask.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(4^(n^2)); Space O(n^2). Recursive DFS marks and unmarks visited cells.

source.label: Rat in a Maze Problem - GeeksforGeeks

problems.name: Unique Paths III
problems.question: Given a grid with start, end, empty cells, and obstacles, return the number of 4-directional paths from start to end that visit every non-obstacle cell exactly once.
problems.constraints: 1 <= m, n <= 20; total cells <= 20 in the original problem.

examples.explanation: Two paths visit all non-obstacle cells.
Four Hamiltonian paths exist.
No path can visit every open cell exactly once.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(4^E); Space O(E). Iterative stack carries position, remaining count, and visited mask.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(4^E); Space O(E). Backtracking marks cells in-place and decrements remaining count.

problems.name: Matchsticks to Square
problems.question: Given matchsticks, return true if they can form a square using every matchstick exactly once.

examples.explanation: Each side can sum to 2.
The total cannot form four equal sides.
Each side gets one stick.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n * 2^n); Space O(2^n). Bitmask DP tracks current side sum modulo target.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(4^n) worst case with strong pruning; Space O(n). Descending backtracking reduces branches.

problems.name: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets
problems.question: Given nums and k, return true if nums can be partitioned into k non-empty subsets with equal sum.

examples.explanation: Each subset can sum to 5.
Total cannot split into equal integer sums.
Two subsets can each sum to 4.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n * 2^n); Space O(2^n). Bitmask DP tracks partial bucket sum modulo target.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(k^n) worst case with pruning; Space O(n + k). Sorted bucket backtracking skips symmetric states.

source.label: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets - LeetCode 698

problems.name: Beautiful Arrangement
problems.question: Given n, count the number of arrangements of 1..n where at position i, either perm[i] is divisible by i or i is divisible by perm[i].

examples.explanation: [1,2] and [2,1] are valid.
Only one arrangement exists.
Three arrangements satisfy the rule.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n * 2^n); Space O(2^n). Iterative DP over used-number masks.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n * 2^n); Space O(2^n + n). Memoized backtracking counts each mask once.
